name: fabfilter-promb-drum-multiband-glue
description: Three-band dynamic clean-up + glue on a drum bus with FabFilter Pro-MB, headless. band_1 tightens boomy LOWS (~30-120 Hz), band_2 tames LOW-MID box (~200-600 Hz) only when it builds, band_3 de-harshes the PRESENCE (~3-9 kHz) on spikes. Each band is a true split — it only touches its own range, leaving the gaps unprocessed (the difference from a fixed-crossover multiband: only the problem zones move). Validated on the Watercolors drum loop.
intended_for: a summed drum bus that is boomy on the loud kicks, builds low-mid mud on busy passages, and spits in the presence band — controlled dynamically without static EQ dulling the steady tone
plugin_build: FabFilter 'Pro-MB.vst3' (renders headless via Pedalboard 0.9.23, no-iLok; 156 enum params; set string enums via the preset harness, not apply-vst-chain's float dict)
notes: Each band sets band_N_state=Enabled AND a NONZERO band_N_range — range is the master 'amount'; at range 0 the band is inert regardless of threshold/ratio (measured).

The three bands do not need to tile: a Pro-MB band only processes between its own low/high crossover; frequencies in the gaps (120-200, 600-3000, >9000, <30) pass UNPROCESSED. That selectivity is the point — fix only the problem zones.

For PARALLEL glue (NY-style) drop the global `mix` below 100 (0..200%) instead of softening each range — measured: mix 50 halved the presence duck (-4.2 -> -2.7 dB). For UPWARD density on a band, switch its dynamics_mode to Expansion with a POSITIVE range (measured: Expansion + range +12 on 3-9k ADDED ~+6 dB presence and raised crest).

attack/release are a normalized 0..100 scale here (not ms); lows get slower attack (15) to keep kick punch, presence gets faster attack (8) to catch spit. Dynamic Phase keeps transients intact. Verify with measure-spectrum: expect lows + low-mids + presence each pulled down only on peaks, mids/air/sub between the bands unchanged.
